metadata.title: STRING THEORY Agent Match Profiles
metadata.description: Detailed personality and taste profiles for 20 top literary agents who are strong fits for an upmarket literary novel with speculative elements
metadata.genre_fit: Upmarket Literary Fiction with Speculative Elements
metadata.themes: Music, physics, grief, inheritance, father-son relationships, buried truth, academic intrigue, cosmic resonance

agent_profiles.name: Ernie Chiara

personality_profile.decision_making: Gut-driven with strong editorial instinct
personality_profile.working_style: Hands-on editorial partner who understands craft from the inside

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Voice above all—they need to feel a distinctive narrative presence immediately
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: The inexplicable rendered in precise, literary prose; a touch of the uncanny grounded in emotional reality
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Generic literary prose, predictable structures, speculative elements that feel grafted on rather than organic
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Reads like a writer—analyzing craft while being swept away by story

style_preferences.prose: Lush but controlled, with rhythm and musicality
style_preferences.pacing: Deliberate but never static; every scene must advance character or mystery
style_preferences.dialogue: Revealing of character, never purely expository
style_preferences.structure: Appreciates formal play when it serves emotional truth

specifically_loves: Claire North's high concepts with literary execution
The 'touch of the inexplicable' in otherwise realistic fiction
Character-driven upmarket fiction with speculative elements
specifically_hates: Speculative elements that feel like genre tourism rather than genuine vision
Plot mechanics that overshadow character
Stories that explain themselves instead of trusting the reader
deal_breakers: First 10 pages that don't establish a unique voice
Queries that describe plot without conveying atmosphere
Comparisons to mega-bestsellers without understanding why
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Chiara writes speculative fiction himself, so he'll immediately recognize and appreciate the musical architecture of your novel—the tempo markings, the four-movement structure of Chapter 1, the Sarabande climax. He's the rare agent who will understand the craft behind the form on a practitioner level.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with voice and the 'inexplicable' element—the frequency, the visions. Emphasize that the speculative grows organically from emotional truth, not the other way around.

agent_profiles.name: Sarah Brooks

personality_profile.decision_making: Responds to harmony and resonance in prose
personality_profile.working_style: Supportive but discerning; values authors who understand their own music

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Listening for rhythm and cadence—prose must sing
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Musicality in language; structure that echoes emotional content
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Prose that's merely functional, stories without internal rhythm
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Reads with an inner ear; text must resonate

style_preferences.prose: Lyrical, rhythmic, with attention to sound and flow
style_preferences.pacing: Tempo matters—understands accelerando, decelerando, rubato in narrative
style_preferences.structure: Appreciates formal musical structures applied to fiction

specifically_loves: Stories with musical themes or structures
Book club fiction with intellectual depth
specifically_hates: Tone-deaf prose
Emotional manipulation without genuine feeling
Structure as gimmick rather than necessity
deal_breakers: First pages with no sense of rhythm
Queries that don't convey the book's emotional frequency
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Brooks studied Music at Nottingham University and holds a piano performance diploma. She will understand your tempo markings, the Sarabande, the four-movement structure of Chapter 1 on a technical level that few agents can match. This is an extraordinary alignment of agent expertise with novel content.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Reference the musical structure explicitly. Mention the tempo markings, the four movements, the Sarabande. She'll recognize immediately that this book was written by someone who understands music from the inside.

agent_profiles.name: Samantha Fabien

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to high-stakes interpersonal dynamics and buried secrets
personality_profile.working_style: Actively engaged; loves untangling complex character motivations

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Immediate immersion in character and stakes
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Academia settings, buried secrets, messy characters, generational trauma
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Quiet character studies without tension, predictable reveals
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Stories must earn their emotional payoffs

style_preferences.pacing: Propulsive but not breathless; stakes must escalate
style_preferences.dialogue: Reveals character through conflict and subtext
style_preferences.structure: Appreciates twists and reveals when earned

specifically_loves: Games or puzzles embedded in narrative
specifically_hates: Stories that play it safe
Characters who lack agency
Resolutions that come too easily
deal_breakers: No clear stakes by page 10
Protagonist without a compelling want
Academia settings that feel generic rather than specific
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Fabien's wishlist reads like it was written for STRING THEORY: 'buried secrets, messy characters, unexpected twists, academia.' The generational trauma between David and his father, the buried ARGO project, the ethical compromise—all hit her exact sweet spot.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the academic suppression angle. Emphasize the buried secret, the twenty-year compromise, the messy relationship with Celeste. The speculative element is the mechanism that forces all these buried things to the surface.

agent_profiles.name: Ashley Lopez

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to unforgettable characters and singular experiences rendered universally
personality_profile.working_style: Editorial collaborator with strong literary instincts

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Movement on the page—prose that creates its own kinetic energy
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Characters who feel unforgettable, experiences that feel singular but speak universally
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Prose that sits still, characters who feel generic
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The sentence itself must generate momentum

style_preferences.prose: Active, kinetic, visually and viscerally engaging
style_preferences.pacing: Driven by sentence rhythm rather than plot mechanics

specifically_hates: Prose that lacks energy
Characters who feel like types rather than people
Speculative elements not rooted in human reality
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without forward momentum
Character introductions that don't create immediate interest
Genre confusion
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Lopez co-founded Pigeon Pages Literary Journal, so she has editorial taste developed outside traditional publishing. Her interest in 'grounded speculative' is exactly your territory—speculative elements rooted in the emotional reality of a man grieving his father while cosmic forces converge.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the grounded emotional reality first, the speculative second. David's grief, his relationship with his father, his failed relationship with Celeste—these are the anchors that make the 68.48 Hz frequency feel real rather than fanciful.

agent_profiles.name: Alexandra Machinist

personality_profile.decision_making: Assesses film/TV potential alongside literary merit
personality_profile.working_style: Strategic career builder with major agency resources

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: High-concept premises executed with literary polish
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Books that are literary but not sellable, or commercial but not well-written
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Can this book break out?

style_preferences.execution: Literary craft applied to commercial premises

specifically_loves: Literary craft applied to genre frameworks
specifically_hates: Quiet literary fiction with no commercial angle
High concepts poorly executed
Books that are hard to pitch in a sentence
deal_breakers: No clear hook by end of query
Genre confusion
First 10 pages that don't establish stakes
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Machinist represents Kevin Kwan, Tomi Adeyemi, and Sabaa Tahir—writers who blend literary quality with breakout commercial potential. Your novel's high concept (a physicist's performance becomes the only surviving video after a solar storm) gives her the hook she needs, while the literary execution gives her the quality.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the hook: the solar storm, the only surviving video, billions watching. Then ground it in the literary execution. She needs to see both the commercial premise and the literary craft.

agent_profiles.name: Bill Clegg

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to pain, memory, and the fragility of self
personality_profile.working_style: Deeply invested in author's vision; editorial collaborator

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Narratives exploring the painful intersections of memory and the fragility of the physical self
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Emotionally distant prose, cleverness without feeling
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Literature should wound and heal

style_preferences.pacing: Unhurried, allowing emotional moments to land

specifically_loves: Narratives about memory and its failures
Stories of physical and psychic fragility
Characters dismantled by their own histories
specifically_hates: Emotionally manipulative prose
Stories that perform suffering without understanding it
Cleverness as a substitute for feeling
deal_breakers: First pages that don't establish emotional stakes
Protagonist who feels observed rather than inhabited
Queries that summarize plot without conveying feeling
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Clegg's interest in 'the painful intersections of memory and the fragility of the physical self' maps directly onto David's dissolution—the frequency invading his body, his career collapsing, his relationships unraveling. The novel's emotional core is exactly what he represents.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with David's internal state—the frequency in his bones, the dissolution, the grief for his father. Let the plot emerge from his experience rather than summarizing events. Make him feel David's fragility.

agent_profiles.name: Chris Parris-Lamb

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to fiction that treats ideas as lived forces
personality_profile.working_style: Champions unconventional projects; values originality

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary fiction that embraces genre-blurring and confrontation
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Safe, conventional narratives
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Ideas should be lived, not just thought

style_preferences.pacing: Varies with project; values risk over convention
style_preferences.ideas: Must be embedded in character experience

specifically_loves: Books that treat ideas as lived forces
specifically_hates: Genre fiction without literary ambition
Literary fiction without forward momentum
Safe bets
deal_breakers: First 10 pages that feel conventional
Queries that don't signal ambition
Projects that fit neatly into categories
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Parris-Lamb's interest in 'fiction that treats ideas as lived forces rather than abstractions' is exactly your methodology. The 68.48 Hz frequency isn't a theoretical concept—it invades David's body, destroys his career, rewrites his reality. The idea is lived.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the lived experience of the idea. Don't explain the frequency—show its effects. Don't theorize about resonance—show David becoming the instrument. Make him feel the idea in his bones, literally.

agent_profiles.name: Julie Barer

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to novels that marry emotional precision with mythic scope
personality_profile.working_style: Long-term career builder for literary authors

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Intimate human stories that feel mythic, universal
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Intimate stories without reach, mythic stories without heart
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The personal and the universal must coexist

style_preferences.scope: Balances intimate moments with larger themes
style_preferences.myth: Echoes of older stories without being derivative

specifically_loves: Stories that feel both personal and universal
specifically_hates: Stories that are all scope and no heart
Stories that are all heart and no reach
Prose that tells readers how to feel
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without emotional immediacy
Protagonist who feels observed rather than inhabited
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Barer's client list (Celeste Ng, Madeline Miller, Ann Patchett) signals her taste for writers who balance intimate emotional truth with larger-than-life stakes. Your novel's father-son core is the intimacy; the solar storm, the frequency, the global broadcast are the mythic scope.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Balance the query. Give her the father-son grief, the failed love with Celeste—and then show how the cosmic stakes amplify rather than overshadow that intimacy. The personal must ground the mythic.

agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Mark represents authors who bend form to interrogate meaning—Maggie Nelson, Ed Park, Sarah Manguso. Your musical structure (four-movement chapters, tempo markings, the novel as symphony) is exactly the kind of formal interrogation he seeks. He'll understand that the form isn't decoration—it's meaning.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Explicitly address the musical architecture. Mention the tempo markings, the four-movement structure, the novel as symphony. He needs to know that the form is intentional and meaning-generating, not arbitrary.

personality_profile.decision_making: Assesses literary merit AND commercial/crossover potential
personality_profile.working_style: Builds careers across formats and territories

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary novels that can break out to wider audiences
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Books that are too quiet to sell or too commercial to respect
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Literary and commercial are not opposites

specifically_hates: Genre fiction without literary merit
Literary fiction without commercial potential
Books that are hard to position

Genre confusion
Stakes that don't escalate
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Witherspoon represents literary novels that also get optioned—exactly your target. The cinematic potential is clear: a physicist whose final performance becomes the only surviving video watched by billions, his disappearance, the global transformation. But the literary execution earns the concept.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the cinematic hook—the solar storm, the only surviving video, billions watching. Then ground it in the literary execution. Show her this is a book that can be discussed at the Frankfurt Book Fair AND pitched to Netflix.

agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Landauer joined Writers House in 2025 after working with Susan Golomb (Franzen, Kushner, Angie Kim). Her philosophy and comparative literature background at Stanford means she'll appreciate the intellectual architecture—the physics, the music theory, the philosophical questions. And she's actively building her list.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with voice and intellectual stakes. She'll appreciate the philosophy/music/physics intersection. And as a newer agent, she's actively looking for debut authors with serious literary ambition.

how_they_read.what_loses_them: Straight genre without literary ambition, straight literary without hook

agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Haywood explicitly seeks 'crossover/hybrid style novels'—which is exactly what STRING THEORY is: literary fiction with speculative elements, a thriller engine, and philosophical depth. Her interest in examinations of 'identity, gender/sexuality and/or racism through a unique lens' connects to your academic suppression/cowardice theme.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the hybrid nature—literary fiction with speculative elements, a thriller structure, philosophical depth. Frame the academic suppression as a critique of how institutions protect themselves by burying inconvenient truths.

agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Your original query cited Marshall's work with Keziah Weir and Erin Morgenstern—authors whose novels 'combine intellectual rigor with a clear, compelling narrative engine.' This is exactly your methodology: using science (string theory, resonance) as a storytelling catalyst, not an end in itself.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Frame the science as catalyst, not content. The 68.48 Hz frequency is what drives David's breakdown, his reckoning, his final act—not an abstract theory to be explained. Show her how the ideas generate story.

agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Brower edited Jeff VanderMeer, so she understands the 'epistemic unease' of Annihilation—the sense that reality is not what we thought, that knowledge itself is destabilizing. Your novel shares that DNA: the buried discovery, the frequency, the dissolution of certainty.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Reference the Annihilation comparison. Frame the novel as literary speculative fiction in the VanderMeer tradition—unease, destabilization, transformation. But emphasize that the emotional core (father, Celeste, grief) keeps it grounded.

The solar storm, the only surviving video, the global broadcast—these are concepts that pitch themselves. But the father-son grief, the failed love with Celeste, the twenty years of silence—that's the literary execution.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the concept—it's strong enough. But quickly ground it in character. Show him that the high concept serves emotional truth, not the other way around.
